neighbours.label: Operating heavy machinery and powered equipment: the slot before or inside machinery/equipment words (tractors and other farm machinery, heavy equipment operators, a bulldozer and its driver), vs the same frames about animals, people or tools without engines
fire: The company hires drivers to operate excavators and other construction machinery.
A forklift and its operator blocked the loading dock for an hour.
The course teaches students to handle heavy equipment safely on site.
Do not drink alcohol before you operate heavy machinery.
The farm replaced its horses with diesel-powered machinery in the 1950s.
Each crane operator must pass a written and practical test.
Combine harvesters and other agricultural machinery fill the fields in August.
The mine uses massive dump trucks and drilling rigs around the clock.
quiet: The company hires cooks to prepare soups and other hot meals.
A mother and her child blocked the doorway for an hour.
The course teaches students to handle difficult customers politely.
Do not drink alcohol before you sign a contract.
The farm replaced its sheep with dairy cows in the 1950s.
Each piano teacher must pass a written and practical test.
Sunflowers and other summer flowers fill the fields in August.
The bakery uses large ovens and mixing bowls around the clock.

predictions: Tokens in operating-machinery phrases reach 0.4-1.0; the same frames about animals, teachers or hand tools stay under 0.1.
notes: Card: top peaks on ' other' before 'farm machinery', ' its' after bulldozer, '-powered' machinery, ' equipment' in 'heavy equipment operators', ' operate' nuclear reactors, 'm|owing' machine; the - pole promotes vehicle/motor/machine.
